description_short.value: Small Tema-based processor of spices, condiments and seasonings, traded on the Ghana Alternative Market; production has depended on a supply agreement with Unifa Brothers since 2025.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Samba Foods Limited financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 (GSE PR 188/2026: report of the directors, principal activities) and GSE PR 342/2025 and PR 038/2026 (memorandum of understanding with Unifa Brothers)

description_full.value: Samba Foods Limited processes food in Tema, specialising in spices, condiments and seasonings; its stated activities also include farming and the export of processed foods. It operates from the West Coast Dyeing Industries compound in Tema's Heavy Industrial Area. The company raised capital through an initial public offer arranged by UniSecurities, and its shares began trading on the Ghana Alternative Market on 12 May 2015; it has 5,976,053 shares in issue. It is very small: income was GHS 1.06 million in 2021, fell to GHS 0.39 million in 2023, and recovered to GHS 1.62 million in 2025. It lost money in 2022, 2023 and 2024, then made a profit of GHS 265,000 in 2025. Accumulated losses of GHS 3.1 million are offset in its equity by a GHS 2.2 million revaluation surplus on its property. After its main packaging machine broke down, it signed a memorandum of understanding with Unifa Brothers in August 2025, under which Unifa supplies raw and packaging materials, replaces the packaging machine and buys finished products made to its standards. The agreement covered 2025 and was extended to 31 March 2026. Dr Leticia Osafo-Addo is managing director and Alexander Banful chairman. No dividend has been recommended in recent years.
